name: Cold waves & winter storms
summary: No major cold wave or winter storm found; no UK Met Office warnings in force on 10 Nov
state: The Met Office had no weather warnings in force on 10 Nov (Met Office), and searches found no top-tier cold or winter-storm warning over a major region or cold outbreak causing outages. Stratospheric polar vortex winds at 60°N fell from 22.13 to 5.44 m/s in eight days to 5 Nov, with a major sudden stratospheric warming forecast (The Watchers); such events can raise the risk of cold spells in Europe weeks later, hence the upward trend.
for_you: No severe cold is forecast now. The Met Office and UKHSA cold-weather health alerts are the official route for UK warnings; older people and those with heart or lung conditions are most exposed when cold spells arrive.
rubric_hit: No top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region (10 Nov): Normal

sources.title: The Watchers — Polar vortex winds at 60°N drop from 22.13 to 5.44 m/s in eight days in rare November disruption

why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.
